post.description: Run every pure compiler stage. Nothing is stored and no SQL is executed.

Compare two schema versions: typed changes, plan changes, ordered steps, guarantee diff.

Pure (no database is touched). The new version is ``new_sql`` or ``alter_sql`` applied to
``old_sql``.
Rebuild and re-run the minimal counterexample of one verdict on fresh sandboxes.

schema.title: Response List Samples Api V1 Samples Get

AISuggestion.title: AISuggestion
AISuggestion.description: The LLM's advisory opinion (never overrides the optimizer).

AccessHint.title: AccessHint
AccessHint.description: User supplied overrides for one relationship (all optional).

ChangeOp.title: ChangeOp
ChangeOp.description: One typed difference between two schema versions.

ConcurrencyResult.title: ConcurrencyResult
ConcurrencyResult.description:
One probe: ``iterations`` racing rounds of ``threads`` writers with a given strategy.

``generated`` runs the helpers exactly as shipped; ``unguarded`` switches their concurrency guards
(lock documents, the atomic array guard) off, or drops the transaction, to show what the same
operations would let through. Zero violations is *test evidence*, not proof; a nonzero count is a
demonstration, reproducible from ``seed``.

ConcurrencySkip.title: ConcurrencySkip
ConcurrencySkip.description: A scenario that could not be probed, and why (never silently missing).

ConditionTrace.title: ConditionTrace
ConditionTrace.description: One condition a rule evaluated and its result (the UI's "Why?" view).

Counterexample.title: Counterexample
Counterexample.description: The smallest data and operation sequence found that shows the behaviours differ.

CounterexampleGap.title: CounterexampleGap
CounterexampleGap.description: Why no counterexample exists for a BROKEN / CHANGED verdict (never silently missing).

CounterexampleStep.title: CounterexampleStep
CounterexampleStep.description: One operation of a counterexample, with what each database did.

DiffRequest.title: DiffRequest
DiffRequest.description: Two schema versions: the new one as DDL or as an ALTER script applied to the old one.

EvidenceCondition.title: EvidenceCondition
EvidenceCondition.description: One condition under which a verdict holds, as data (the text is for humans).

EvidenceUpgrade.title: EvidenceUpgrade
EvidenceUpgrade.description: A verification run raised an UNVERIFIED verdict to TESTED, and on what basis.

Flip.title: Flip
Flip.description: A weight change that turns the decision around.

Fragility.title: Fragility
Fragility.description: How sensitive a decision is to the tunable weights (see optimizer/sensitivity.py).

PlacementChange.title: PlacementChange
PlacementChange.description: A verdict whose status changed between the initial and final pass.

PlanChange.title: PlanChange
PlanChange.description: A relationship whose placement differs between the two versions.

RenameCandidate.title: RenameCandidate
RenameCandidate.description: A drop + add that looks like a rename. Never applied without confirmation.

RuleInput.title: RuleInput
RuleInput.description: A value the rule consulted ("Why?" trace): placement decision, option or node.

VerdictChange.title: VerdictChange
VerdictChange.description: A guarantee verdict that differs between the old and the new version.

WorkloadSpec.title: WorkloadSpec
WorkloadSpec.description:
Per-query relative frequencies (a sidecar ``workload.yaml`` or the API option).

Keys are query ids (``q1``, ``q2``, ... in file order). A ``-- @freq N`` comment before a
statement
sets the same thing inline; an explicit entry here wins over a comment. Unlisted queries weigh
``default_freq`` (1).
